Why cant Washington build a website?

From the article:

Rather than thinking about the digital sphere as a chance to improve the way they do business, government institutions have mostly treated it as a new, online overlay to their pre-digital business practices. Imagine if your bank were operating with the infrastructure available to it in 1972. Would you still be a customer?

Because:

  • ARIA
  • ADA
  • committees
  • subcommittees
  • everyone's grandma's opinions
  • funding
  • pecking order

And every goddamn red tape you could ever imagine. It's analysis paralysis at government scale.

Disjointed collaboration among numerous contractors almost never works on a large scale. If there were ever a time to put all your eggs in one basket it's this kind of project. Find a good team that has the skill to put it together top to bottom and let them do their thing.
As a former employee of a firm that does public sector contracting... this comment is too close to the truth.

Because they don't understand the Internet; the same people who see Netflix Users as Freeloaders, thought SOPA was a good idea, and are against Net Neutrality aren't the best people to build a website, anymore than hiring a bunch of cavemen to oversee technicians implement network infrastructure.

If the people who are doing it (build a website) can gain money now, and get paid later to fix what they messed up, they're going to do just that. In fact, it'll never be right, just so they have something to fix.

It's far simpleR that this article portrays. Governments tend to create massive projects that are delivered after years. Look at the British NHS software cockup, by the time the project was finished the requirements had changed and it wasn't fit for purpose. To use jargon they are too waterfall and not agile.

Thankfully the UK government, in a unusually sensible move, changed to agile. Every government contact now has to be agile. They even made a brilliant site https://www.gov.uk/service-manual/agile anybody looking at a career in IT should have a read.

Most good websites start small and then scale but government websites are expected to start life as complete. Look at voat it was given a chance to develop initial without a high number of users and then scaled up to its current size adding and testing along the way, had it it been expected to launch in its current state with this many users it would have been a colossal failure and everyone would have bailed before it got anywhere.
